priority.override_reason: Ranks 1 through 7 are closed by their current profiles and consumed frame, object, RegExp, string, or helper-graph mechanisms. A fresh rank-8 date-format-xparb profile has 1,575 useful main-thread samples: its native-constructor caller-environment setup and writeback total only about twelve samples, while the remaining boxed-String body and generic string concatenation require substantially higher-cost representation or escape-analysis work and the prior shared StringData attempt is closed. The fresh rank-9 date-format-tofte profile instead exposes a distinct low-cost boundary: a native Date constructor invoked beneath cached direct eval snapshots and writes back a dynamic caller environment even though native constructors, like the already-generalized native call path, do not inherit caller lexical bindings. This is not the rejected direct-construction realm-context alias, which concerned user-bytecode constructors whose call_env and realm_env both allocate the same empty child frame; here the current native path demonstrably takes frame_call_env and apply_env around the constructor body.

mechanism.summary: When a bytecode Construct operation has resolved an unbound native Function target, invoke construct_function with a realm-only CallEnv instead of snapshotting and later writing back the active caller frame, mirroring the existing frame-independent native-call rule.
mechanism.generality: Admission depends only on the resolved constructor representation: a directly resolved Function with a native implementation and no bound target uses the current realm-only environment. Native constructors still receive the same target, newTarget, arguments, shared realm, module host, agent context, prototype lookup, and callback behavior. Proxy, bound, user-bytecode, class, derived, Reflect.construct forwarding, and non-constructable targets retain the current call_env path. No source text, benchmark identity, function name, argument value, iteration count, checksum, or result is inspected.
semantic_risks: preserving newTarget installation and restoration plus prototype lookup, including replaced native-constructor prototypes and cross-realm prototype markers
preserving argument coercion and native-constructor callbacks whose user functions capture caller or eval-created cells
preserving shared realm writes and refreshing sloppy-global-backed caller slots after construction
keeping Proxy, bound-function, user-bytecode, derived-class, and Reflect.construct forwarding on paths that may execute arbitrary constructor code
preserving abrupt completion and thrown-value identity while avoiding caller frame writeback only for the frame-independent native target

profile_evidence.shared_cost: Of 2,178 useful main-thread samples, the native Date construction reached from cached eval has 19 samples in construct_callee caller-environment materialization and 208 disjoint samples in apply_call_env after the constructor body. These 227 samples, or 10.4 percent, are the snapshot and writeback work removed by selecting the existing realm-only environment before an unbound native constructor. The 49-sample construct_function body, prototype selection, Date parsing, receiver allocation, and all user code remain unchanged.
